paragraphs.text: Designers should code, and engineers should design.

For years, titles decided who could touch what. Everything in between was a handoff: a rebuild, a round of screenshots, a backlog of small fixes nobody had time for. That handoff is where products lose their quality.
AI removed the reason to keep the roles apart. In
, designers working in development doubled to 41% in a year, and developers doing design rose to 60%.
found half of designers now ship code to production.
Ownership did not move with it. At
, every designer shipped a pull request in a month, and each was reviewed like any other code.
So an engineer's design is an idea until a designer makes it production ready. A designer's pull request is a start until an engineer polishes it.
That is not a handoff. Both people work on the same thing, so nothing gets rebuilt.
Anyone can start anything now. The owner still finishes it.
